paper.title: Learning to Optimize Via Posterior Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Finitely many actions (Bayesian, arbitrary prior, rewards in [0,1])
unmapped: Arbitrary prior over reward functions; actions need not be modeled independently
settings.definition_quote: We consider in this section a problem with $|\mathcal{A}| < \infty$ actions and rewards satisfying $R_t \in [0,1]$ for all $t$ almost surely. ... we make no further assumptions on the class of reward functions $\mathcal{F}$ or on the prior distribution over $\theta$.

unmapped: Parameter norm bounded by c1 and feature norm bounded by c2 (not necessarily known)
Action sets A_t are possibly random subsets of A
settings.definition_quote: If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle$ ..., $\sup_{\rho \in \Theta} \|\rho\|_2 \leq c_1$, and $\sup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \|\phi(a)\|_2 \leq c_2$, and for each $t$, $R_t - f_{\theta}(A_t)$ conditioned on $(H_t, A_t, \theta)$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian

unmapped: Rewards in [0,C] for a constant C (not [0,1])
Link function strictly increasing, continuously differentiable; ratio r of max/min slope enters bound
Exists a_1..a_d with sum phi phi^T >= lambda I
settings.definition_quote: If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=g(\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle)$ for some strictly increasing continuously differentiable function $g$, $\sup_{\rho} \|\rho\|_2 \leq c_1$, $\sup_{a} \|\phi(a)\|_2 \leq c_2$, $\mathcal{A}_t = \mathcal{A}$ for all $t$, $\sum_{i=1}^{d} \phi(a_i) \phi(a_i)^T \succeq \lambda I$ ..., and $R_t \in [0,C]$

unmapped: Reward function drawn from a Gaussian process prior with marginal variances bounded by 1
settings.definition_quote: If $\mathcal{A}$ is finite, $\left( f_\theta(a):  a\in \mathcal{A} \right)$ follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution with marginal variances bounded by $1$, ... $\{R_t-f_{\theta}(A_t)\}$ is an iid sequence of zero-mean Gaussian random variables with variance $\sigma^{2}$

settings.name_in_paper: General function classes (bounded reward functions, sub-Gaussian noise)
unmapped: Known function class F with f(a) in [0,C]
Complexity measured via eluder dimension and Kolmogorov dimension
settings.definition_quote: For all $f \in \mathcal{F}$ and $a \in \mathcal{A}$, $f(a) \in [0,C]$. ... For all $t \in \mathbb{N}$, $R_t-f_{\theta}(A_t)$ conditioned on $(H_t, \theta, A_t)$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian.

algorithms.name: Posterior sampling with initial designed exploration (pi^IPS_{a_1..a_d})

source.label: prop:finite
source.quote: If $|\mathcal{A}|=K<\infty$ and $R_t \in [0,1]$, then for any $T\in \mathbb{N}$ \mathrm{BayesRegret}(T, \pi^{\mathrm{PS}}) \leq 2\min\{K, T\}+4\sqrt{K T(2+6\log(T))}.

results.notes: Holds for arbitrary prior; PS does not use T so marked anytime.

source.label: prop:linear
source.quote: Fix positive constants $\sigma$, $c_1$, and $c_2$. If ... then $${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) = O(d \log T \sqrt{T}),$$

results.notes: Proof only sketched (derived from Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2011 analysis).

symbols.E_sqrt_s0: E[sqrt(||theta||_0)], expected square root of number of nonzero components of theta under the prior

results.notes: Sparse linear bound derived from Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2012; proof sketch only.

symbols.r_g: ratio sup g'/inf g' of the link function slope over actions and parameters

extra_assumptions: strictly increasing continuously differentiable link g

source.label: prop:generalizedLinear
source.quote: ... then $${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm IPS}_{a_1,\ldots,a_d}\right) = O(r d \log^{3/2} T \sqrt{T}),$$ where $r=\sup_{\rho,a}g'(\langle \phi(a), \rho\rangle) / \inf_{\rho,a}g'(\langle \phi(a),\rho\rangle)$.

results.notes: Derived from Filippi et al. 2010; proof sketch only.

extra_assumptions: iid Gaussian noise with variance sigma^2

source.quote: If $\mathcal{A}$ is finite, ... then $${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right)\leq 1+2\sqrt{T \gamma_T \ln\left(1+\sigma^{-2}\right)^{-1} \ln\left(\frac{(T^2+1) \left| \mathcal{A}\right|} {\sqrt{2\pi}} \right)}$$ for all $T \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.notes: K = |A|; paper's sigma is noise std. Interpreted ln(1+sigma^-2)^{-1} as 1/ln(1+sigma^-2).

bound.expression_latex: 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+ 16\sigma \sqrt{  {\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F},  T^{-1} \right) \left(1+o(1)+{\rm dim}_K\left(\mathcal{F} \right) \right) \log(T) T}

symbols.C_rew: uniform bound on reward functions, f(a) in [0,C]

extra_assumptions: f(a) in [0,C] for all f in F

source.label: prop: risk bound
source.quote: For any fixed class of functions $\mathcal{F}$, $${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+ 16\sigma \sqrt{  {\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F},  T^{-1} \right) \left(1+o(1)+{\rm dim}_K\left(\mathcal{F} \right) \right) \log(T) T}$$ for all $T\in \mathbb{N}$.

results.notes: Proposition numbering inferred. Contains an o(1) term; C renamed C_rew to avoid clash with corruption budget.

symbols.C_rew: uniform bound on reward functions, f(a) in [0,C]
symbols.N_F: cardinality |F| of the finite function class

source.label: prop: risk bound
source.quote: Further, if $\mathcal{F}$ is finite then $${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+8\sigma\sqrt{2{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right) \log\left(2\left|\mathcal{F}\right|T\right)T},$$ for all $T \in \mathbb{N}$.

Then, ${\rm dim}_E(\mathcal{F}, \epsilon) = O(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ and ${\rm dim}_K(\mathcal{F}) = O(d)$. Proposition \ref{prop: risk bound} therefore yields an $O(d\sqrt{T}\log(T))$ Bayesian regret bound.

results.notes: Specialization of general eluder-dimension bound, stated in an Example.

symbols.r_g: ratio of max to min slope of the link function g

source.quote: Then, ${\rm dim}_K(\mathcal{F}) = O(d)$ and ${\rm dim}_E(\mathcal{F}, \epsilon) = O(r^2 d\log(r \epsilon))$ ... Proposition \ref{prop: risk bound} yields an $O(rd\sqrt{T} \log (rT))$ Bayesian regret bound.

results.notes: Applies to standard PS (no initial exploration). Setting s3 used though the noise assumption here is sub-Gaussian rather than bounded and A_t need not be fixed.
